projects.name: End of 2026 Spanish high-speed speed limits
projects.description: Temporary Adif speed restrictions imposed after the January 2026 Adamuz accident add ~30 min to Madrid–Barcelona and ~15 min to Madrid–Valencia.
projects.status: Restrictions extended to the end of 2026; normal running assumed from 2027.

projects.name: Deutschlandtakt (stages to 2030 and 2035)
projects.officialTarget: Staged; next stage 2030 (not a completion date)
projects.description: Germany's integrated national clock-face timetable, delivered through staged infrastructure upgrades. Modelled as −5% on German links by 2030 and a further −3% by 2035.
projects.status: Official FAQ: 2030 is a stage, not a completion date; target timetable being revised against the 2040 forecast.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Named only as the "guiding political principle"; no dates or figures. The generic speed-up used here may partly overlap named German projects.

projects.name: Deutschlandtakt (full target network)
projects.officialTarget: Target network aligned to the 2040 forecast
projects.description: Full target network including new lines on bottleneck corridors. Modelled as a further −4% on German links.
projects.status: No official completion year.

projects.name: Stuttgart 21
projects.description: New underground through-station and approach tunnels, fully exploiting the Wendlingen–Ulm line. Stated saving ~15 min for through trains (e.g. Stuttgart–Munich, Paris–Munich).
projects.status: DB reset (June 2026): December 2026 dropped; airport station Dec 2030, main station Dec 2031, final stages to 2033.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: States "Travel time reduction approx. 15 min" (used here). Its Dec 2026 date is superseded; the TT2030 draft no longer lists S21 before TT2030, consistent with Dec 2031.

projects.name: Karlsruhe–Offenburg new line: Rastatt section
projects.description: Continuous four tracks between Karlsruhe and Offenburg with 250 km/h running through the Rastatt tunnel; ~3 min saved on Rhine Valley long-distance services (Frankfurt/Karlsruhe–Basel, Strasbourg/Paris–Stuttgart/Munich).
projects.status: Listed for TT2027 (Dec 2026) in the RNE Common Capacity Strategy TT2030; not yet reflected in the Oct–Nov 2026 timetable samples used for the 2026 baseline, so it counts from 2030.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: States "approx. 3 min in long distance traffic"; 250 km/h; TT2027.

projects.name: Lyon–Turin base tunnel
projects.description: 57.5 km base tunnel under the Alps; Lyon–Turin ~1h55 and Paris–Milan ~4h with full access lines.
projects.status: About 30% complete; 49.8 of 164 km of tunnels dug (Oct 2026). Date fixed in the EU implementing decision (July 2025).

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Lists the base tunnel as "Phase 4 beyond 2030"; the existing Fréjus line has tunnel-maintenance closures 2026–2030.

projects.name: Brenner Base Tunnel
projects.description: 55 km tunnel Innsbruck–Fortezza; cuts ~1 hour from Munich–Verona.
projects.status: New delay announced 20 October 2026 (was 2032): works finish 2033, then a year of commissioning; cost ~€11.7bn.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: No opening date given; the southern access Fortezza–Ponte Gardena is listed for 2029 ("reducing travel time", no figure).

projects.name: Semmering Base Tunnel
projects.description: 27 km tunnel on Austria's Southern Railway. ÖBB states Vienna–Graz in under 2 hours (now 2h26) and Vienna–Klagenfurt 2h45 (now 3h10), i.e. ~25 min off journeys south of Vienna (Venice, Ljubljana, Zagreb).
projects.status: Excavation finished 2024; rail systems being fitted.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Confirms Dec 2029 and "reduction in journey time" (no figure).

projects.name: Fehmarn Belt fixed link
projects.officialTarget: No official year; road ≥2031, rail later (≥2032)
projects.description: 18 km immersed tunnel Denmark–Germany; Hamburg–Copenhagen ~2h30.
projects.status: Two-stage opening announced 17 May 2026: road first, rail once German land works are ready (at least 2032). New schedule due after first elements are sunk.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Banedanmark plans the Danish landside line (Ringsted–Rødby) ready in 2029; through rail service still depends on the tunnel and German works (≥2032, kept).

projects.name: CPK high-speed rail (Warsaw–Łódź and extensions)
projects.description: Poland's "Y" high-speed line via the new airport. Stated times: Warsaw–Łódź 40 min (2032); Warsaw–Poznań and Warsaw–Wrocław ~1h40, Łódź–Poznań and Łódź–Wrocław ~1h (2035).
projects.status: Stage 1 Warsaw–airport–Łódź 2032; extension to Poznań and Wrocław 2035. Tenders for line sections under way.

projects.name: Montpellier–Perpignan new line (LNMP)
projects.description: Missing high-speed link between France and Spain. Phase 1 saves ~20 min, phase 2 a further ~40 min on Paris/Lyon/Marseille–Barcelona.
projects.status: Steering committee of 3 July 2026 confirmed works start by end of 2029; phase 2 date "being consolidated".

projects.name: Rail Baltica
projects.officialTarget: Phase 1 (single track) 2030; Polish section to Warsaw undated
projects.description: New standard-gauge line Tallinn–Riga–Kaunas/Vilnius–Polish border. Stated times: Tallinn–Riga 1h42, Riga–Vilnius 1h54, Riga–Kaunas ~1h32, Vilnius–Kaunas 38 min; Vilnius–Kaunas–Warsaw 3h52 once the Polish section is done.
projects.status: EU milestone: single-track electrified line Tallinn–LT/PL border by 2030 (RB Rail CEO calls this demanding). Polish Ełk–border section still in design.

projects.name: Naples–Bari high-speed/high-capacity line
projects.description: Naples–Bari ~2h, Rome–Bari ~3h.
projects.status: Naples–Cancello open; Telese–Vitulano and Orsara–Bovino 2028; Apice–Hirpinia and Hirpinia–Orsara 2030.

projects.name: Basque Y high-speed network
projects.description: High-speed triangle Bilbao–Vitoria–San Sebastián linking to Irun; Bilbao–San Sebastián ~50 min.
projects.status: March 2026: track bed to be finished "in less than a year"; officials avoid giving dates. 2030 is this tool's estimate.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Not mentioned by ADIF; SNCF Réseau lists a double standard-gauge track Hendaye–Irun for 2029.

projects.name: Ostlänken (East Link)
projects.description: New high-speed line Järna–Linköping (Torvinge); saves ~35 min on Stockholm–Copenhagen.
projects.status: Under the 2026–2037 national plan the line ends at Torvinge, east of Linköping.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Trafikverket gives no opening date; only Norrköping C station works 2030–2036.

projects.name: HS2 Phase 1 (London–Birmingham)
projects.description: New line London–Birmingham. HS2 states Old Oak Common–Birmingham Curzon Street ~42–45 min and Euston–Curzon Street 49 min (now 1h17–1h19). Modelled from 2039 as 55 min to central London (Old Oak + Elizabeth line). Manchester/Scotland trains only gain once Euston and the Handsacre link open (2040–2043, beyond this tool's horizon).
projects.status: Reset of 19 May 2026: first services Old Oak Common–Birmingham May 2036–Oct 2039; Euston and full scheme 2040–2043; top speed cut to 320 km/h.

projects.name: Brescia–Verona high-speed line
projects.description: Completes high speed from Milan to Verona; ~12 min saved.
projects.status: Slipped from February 2026; trial runs since June 2026.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Dated 2027 ("running times reduction", no figure); the TT2029 edition said Dec 2026.

projects.name: Verona–Vicenza–Padua high-speed line
projects.officialTarget: Verona–Vicenza 2027; Vicenza crossing Sept 2033; Vicenza–Padua undated
projects.description: Extends high speed towards Venice; Milan–Venice ~1h50 when complete.
projects.status: Lot 1 works finished (Aug 2026); lot 3 Vicenza–Padua only funded for final design.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Dates the Verona–Vicenza section 2027, yet lists a line closure for the same works in 2029–2030; Vicenza–Padua not mentioned. 2033 kept.

projects.name: Mediterranean Corridor: Valencia–Castellón–Tarragona
projects.description: Gauge conversion and upgrades; Barcelona–Valencia ~2h15.
projects.status: Closure dates for the gauge change still being set. No dedicated project page; link is an Adif press note.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: ADIF confirms the Castellón–Tarragona gauge conversion but gives no date or journey time.

projects.name: GPSO: Bordeaux–Toulouse high-speed line
projects.description: New 222 km line. Stated: Bordeaux–Toulouse 1h05 (now 2h20) and Paris–Toulouse 3h10 (now 4h35).
projects.status: May 2026 State–local deal releases ~€500m for tenders; COI advisers call 2032/33 very hard to meet.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Speed-increase phases dated 2031 (Toulouse end) and TT2032; no time figure.

projects.name: Prague–Brno high-speed line
projects.description: First Czech high-speed line. Správa železnic states Prague–Brno ~1h (now 2h36), so ~1h30 off every train via Brno (Prague–Vienna, –Bratislava, –Budapest, Berlin–Vienna).
projects.status: Construction from ~2030, 5–6 years to build (Správa železnic interview); the transport minister has said high-speed trains will come "first in 2040". No formal date.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: Prague-end connection works (Běchovice–Libeň) run 10/2029–10/2035; no date or time for the line.

projects.name: Berlin–Dresden 200 km/h upgrade
projects.description: Upgrade to 200 km/h. DB states Berlin–Dresden 80 min (fastest today ~94 min), ~14 min off all Berlin/Hamburg–Prague/Brno/Vienna/Bratislava trains.
projects.status: Total closure Apr 2028–Dec 2029 (RNE); last section delayed to end of 2033.

projects.name: Plzeň–Domažlice upgrade (Prague–Munich line)
projects.officialTarget: Plzeň–Stod section after total closure Jan 2028–Jun 2030
projects.description: New 200 km/h alignment Plzeň–Stod; Správa železnic states Plzeň–Domažlice ~35 min instead of ~45.
projects.status: RNE Common Capacity Strategy TT2030 lists the Plzeň–Stod total closure Jan 2028–Jun 2030.

projects.name: Danish Funen upgrades: Vestfyn new line + Ringsted–Odense 200 km/h
projects.description: Danish Transport Ministry: Vestfyn new line ~6 min faster Odense–Jutland; 200 km/h Ringsted–Odense ~5 min faster. ~11 min off Copenhagen–Jutland (Hamburg–Copenhagen via Jutland until Fehmarn opens).
projects.status: Banedanmark capacity strategy TT2030: Vestfyn opens end of 2029; 180→200 km/h Ringsted–Slagelse, Nyborg–Odense 2028–2029.

projects.name: Hanover–Berlin line rebuild (closure Oct 2026–Dec 2027)
projects.description: The Hanover–Berlin high-speed line is closed for general renovation, adding ~70 min to Hanover/Cologne/Amsterdam–Berlin trains. Normal running (Hanover–Berlin ~1h36, Cologne–Berlin ~4h20, Amsterdam–Berlin ~5h42) is assumed after reopening.
projects.status: Closure Oct 2026–Dec 2027 (RNE: Lehrte–Berlin general renovation 2027).

projects.name: New line Frankfurt–Mannheim (NBS Rhein/Main–Rhein/Neckar)
projects.description: New 300 km/h line; DB states Frankfurt–Mannheim 29 instead of 38 min, i.e. −9 min on trains from Frankfurt/Cologne/Hamburg/Paris towards Stuttgart, Basel and Zurich.
projects.status: Federal government report (July 2026): full commissioning expected 2037.

projects.name: Gäubahn: Pfaffensteig tunnel (Stuttgart–Zurich)
projects.description: New 11 km tunnel linking the Gäubahn to Stuttgart Airport and the S21 network; DB states ~15 min shorter Stuttgart–Zurich.
projects.status: Symbolic construction start 12 Oct 2026; opening Dec 2033 in the City of Stuttgart staging plan (June 2026).

projects.name: Budapest–Belgrade railway
projects.description: Rebuilt 160–200 km/h line. Hungarian government: Budapest–Kelebia 90 min; Serbian government: Belgrade–Budapest 2h40 (first through trains from Dec 2026 at 3h17).
projects.status: Hungarian section finished Jan 2026; freight since Feb 2026; passenger start slipped to 13 Dec 2026.

projects.name: Ligne nouvelle Provence Côte d'Azur (phases 1–2)
projects.description: Underground through station at Marseille Saint-Charles; stated −20 min for trains crossing Marseille (e.g. Paris/Lyon–Nice TGVs, which today reverse there).
projects.status: Phases 3–4 (new Marseille–Toulon–Nice sections) around 2040, no stated times yet.

projects.name: Athens–Thessaloniki line restoration (OSE/ERGOSE)
projects.officialTarget: No firm year (estimate); new trains by end of 2027
projects.description: ERGOSE states Athens–Thessaloniki will take 3 h once works are complete (5h12 in the 2026 works timetable; ~4h15 before 2023).
projects.status: Reconstruction after the 2023 Tempi accident continues through 2026; 2028 is this tool's estimate.

projects.name: Porto–Vigo high-speed line (LAV Porto–Valença)
projects.description: IP: direct Porto–Vigo in 50 min (now ~2h30–3h30).
projects.status: Phase 1 tenders 2027; environmental assessments submitted mid-2026.

projects.name: New line Dresden–Prague (Erzgebirge base tunnel)
projects.description: BMV: Dresden–Prague from 2.5 h to 1 h. Beyond this tool's 2040 horizon.
projects.status: Bundestag approved further planning May 2026; construction from Dec 2032.

projects.name: Lisbon–Madrid link (Évora–Elvas + Madrid–Extremadura HSL)
projects.officialTarget: Évora–Elvas end 2026/early 2027; Madrid–Lisbon direct "by 2030"; high speed 2034
projects.description: Lisbon–Badajoz under 2h (Évora–Elvas), a direct Lisbon–Madrid train (~5h, 2030), then high speed (~3h, 2034).
projects.status: Évora–Elvas track complete (Jan 2026), signalling/certification pending. Madrid–Extremadura: Plasencia–Badajoz open since 2022, other sections in works or design.

rneCapacityStrategy.text: ADIF lists only the Mérida–Aljucén doubling (to 2030); no Badajoz–Elvas works, and 0 long-distance border paths/h planned.

projects.name: Lisbon–Porto high-speed line
projects.description: New high-speed line. IP: after phase 2 (~2033) a non-stop Porto–Lisbon train takes 1h19 (now 2h39); the headline 1h15 needs phase 3, with no date.
projects.status: Porto–Oiã under concession (July 2025); Oiã–Soure re-tendered Jan 2026; Carregado–Lisbon later.
